div.span: Summary of Secondary Conclusions

div.style: text-align: left;
text-align: left;
text-align: left;
text-align: left;
text-align: left;
text-align: left;

font.span: God is atemporal/eternal: experiencing no past, present, or future.

span.font: - God is aspatial/immaterial: not being composed, caused, or governed by physical processes.

span.b: God wanted the universe to be created exactly as it is.

div.font:
- Destruction is an easier task than creation and maintaining order.
- God could have more easily destroyed this universe than to have created it. - God is not surprised by what He creates.

font.span: God intentionally created us with a purpose.

div.style: text-align: left;
div.span: God doesn't change His mind, in the sense of learning of a better approach to something.

div.style: text-align: left;
div.span: - Reality does not contain contradictions.

div.style: text-align: left;

span.b: God's will is the fundamental material of reality.

div.style: font-size: 8px; text-align: left;
div.span: The universe's existence is not a one-time event, but a continuous processes.

div.style: text-align: left;
div.span: The purpose of our [phenomenal] senses is to translate God's will into our awareness.

div.style: font-size: 8px; text-align: left;
div.span: - R
eality is not self-sustaining or accidental.

div.style: font-size: 8px; text-align: left;
div.span: - The consistent laws of nature we observe are a direct reflection of God's unchanging will.

div.style: font-size: 8px; text-align: left;
div.span: - The dependence of reality on God's will is why we can
infer His necessary properties from its structure.

div.style: font-size: 8px; text-align: left;
text-align: left;
text-align: left;

div.span: God has complete power over us.

div.style: text-align: center;
text-align: left;
font-size: 1px;

span.b: Truth and proper reason correspond with God's will.

div.style: text-align: left;
div.span: To implement proper reasoning is to align our minds with His will.

font.span: To understand a truth is to understand an aspect of God's sustained, willed expression.

div.style: font-size: 1px; text-align: left;
div.span: Rationalizing falsehood is an act that does not correspond with God's will.

div.style: font-size: 1px; text-align: left;
div.span: God is not the author of confusion.

div.style: font-size: 1px; text-align: left;
text-align: left;
font-size: 1px;

span.b: God gave us a will to choose the values that govern how we live our lives.

div.span: God allows us to pursue good or evil as we wish.

div.style: font-size: 1px;
div.font: - God
div.span: allows us the capacity to pursue falsehood if we choose to use our reason improperly.
Our wills "seek permission" from God to manifest in reality.

div.style: font-size: 1px;
div.span: - Our wills are distinct from God (ie. still contingent) and from temporal reality (ie. are atemporal).

font.span: - The causal relationship between God's will and ours is a paradox as we can't comprehend atemporality.

div.style: font-size: 1px;
div.span: Destiny and predestiny refer to the same concept, differing only on temporal/atemporal perspective.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 413px; height: 1px; padding-top: 618px; margin-left: 412px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: 9. Any True religion corresponds to the purpose that God created us for.

div.font: - God has an ontological will and a prescriptive will.
- God wants us to freely pursue the Truth.
- Proper reason filters out falsehood and converges towards the true understanding of reality.
- Some decisions are objectively better than others.
- Only one set of fundamental claims corresponds to the singular, consistent reality of God's will.
- A "religion" is a way of life that is governed by a set of beliefs and values.
- A "True religion" prescribes the way of life that achieves our God-given purpose.
- Any True religion will be fundamentally founded on using proper reason to believe in God.
- The True religion transcends comfort and culture, guiding towards truth and what is right.
- "Faith" is a form of reason in which the foundational premise relies on trustworthiness or knowledge rather than empirical observation.
- A religion that fundamentally reduces to a leap of faith against/without reason has no mechanism to distinguish itself from a well-crafted falsehood that appeals to the same emotions or desires.
- Reality corresponds more closely with a test than a punishment.

font.b: 10. The True religion corresponds with reality.

div.font: - An exception doesn't disprove the rule; it highlights the existence of a "higher" law that encompasses both.
- A "miracle" is, fundamentally, a unique phenomenon that contradicts human capacity to replicate it.
- True miracles must be distinguishable from false (manmade, deceptive) miracles.
- A mystery is a paradoxical gap in our knowledge that is beyond our limited human comprehension.
- A contradiction is where the distinguishable difference between two things is also shared by them.
- Both mysteries and contradictions appear as profoundly deep concepts, yet are distinguishable on their correspondence with reality.
- Mysteries cause reflection on our own limits, relative to God's ultimate power and transcendence.
- Contradictions require infinite justifications, fundamentally appealing to emotion instead of proper reason.
- The True religion does not demand belief in contradictions.

- If a religion has no distinguishing factor between mysteries and contradictions, then it is fundamentally indistinguishable from a false religion (as falsehoods now can be portrayed as mysteries without detection).
- Subjectivity is a product of imperfect perception, not reality itself.

font.b: 11. The True religion is distinguishable from false religions.

div.font: - The True religion is necessarily both internally and externally consistent to reality, without any contradictions.
- We can use tools like source, logical, and empirical evaluation to filter the True religion from the false one.
- Humble, iterative reasoning necessarily converges on the Truth, allowing discoverability without coercion.
- The consistency of the True religion necessarily reflects God's consistency when it comes to Truth.
- False religions will inevitably contradict reality at a fundamental level.
- Faith is blind when reason isn't used to verify the source's trustworthiness and reliability.
- God tests us (in the pursuit of Truth) by means of others (how they treat us).

font.b: 12. The True religion is accessible to everyone (whether they seek it or not).

div.font: - The True religion must be founded on principles that transcend language and culture.
- The primary "scripture" of the True religion is embedded in reality itself: universally discoverable and attainable.
- Humble, accumulative, iterative reasoning necessarily converges on the Truth while filtering out falsehoods.
- God does not hold us accountable for a capacity that we can't achieve.
- Reason, reflection, and humility are universally available to anyone who is willing to pursue the Truth.
